description: Where a pick-up is put down (PL.pickup-placement, U89(3), U49(3); the P6 cell's M4): given its authored spot, the obstacles by kind, the clearance per kind and the search pattern, the settled spot and the side it is walked up to from, or a refusal with a code. Metres on core's ground plane (x, z); heights are y. Data in, decision out: no navmesh (the caller states where the ground is walkable).
sources: unreal feat/p6-unreal 29c37ab, Source/InsimulRuntime/Private/InsimulVillageProps.cpp 513–790 (the interim settle every constant is measured from, U89(3)); unreal's settle is not changed by this corpus
numerics: Runners compute in IEEE-754 double precision (Unreal: double, as its FVector is). The tolerance covers reported numbers, not decisions: several cases decide exactly on a boundary (a clearance of exactly 0 is clear; a point exactly on a walkable area's edge is walkable), each exact in binary and in Unreal's whole centimetres, so a float32 runner may decide them the other way.

contract.units: metres on the ground plane {x, z}; y is up

frames.unreal: left-handed, z up; core (x, z) = Unreal (X, Y) ÷ 100 and core y = Unreal Z ÷ 100 (cm → m); +x toward +z is +X toward +Y, clockwise seen from above
frames.godot: right-handed, y up; core (x, y, z) = Godot (x, y, z) in metres; +x toward +z is clockwise seen from above
frames.unity: left-handed, y up; core (x, y, z) = Unity (x, y, z) in metres; +x toward +z is counter-clockwise seen from above
frames.babylon: left-handed, y up; core (x, y, z) = Babylon (x, y, z) in metres; +x toward +z is counter-clockwise seen from above

roadDefaultWidthM.source: VP:630 (… : 3.0) * 50.0, a width in metres halved in cm

navSnapM.source: VP:712–713 (engine-side: the walkable test core does not run)

cullRadiusM.source: VP:719 Near(P.At, 2100.0) cm (engine-side: core does not cull)

deviations.unreal: no clear spot within 20 m: draws the pick-up at the clearest walkable spot and logs "NO clear spot" (VP:744–758)
deviations.core: refuses with `no-clear-spot`, carrying that same spot as `clearest`
deviations.why: the ruling asks for a decision or a refusal with a code; an engine that still draws the pick-up draws it at `clearest`, as Unreal does

deviations.unreal: a spot is walkable when the navmesh projects it within 0.3 m (VP:709–714)
deviations.core: the caller states the walkable areas (`walkable`), or passes a predicate; absent, every spot is walkable
deviations.why: core has no navmesh; the engine binds its own query, as the pass-by rule takes `room` from the caller

deviations.unreal: each search point is re-grounded by a line trace (VP:733–734) and the 0.15–1.5 m height band is read at that point's ground
deviations.core: the band is read at the authored spot's ground (`groundY`) for every point
deviations.why: core works on (x, z) with no terrain; on a village's ground the height within 20 m changes little against a 1.35 m band

deviations.unreal: statics are culled to 21 m of the authored spot first (VP:719), for speed over tens of thousands of instances
deviations.why: the settled spot is the same (a culled static is more than 1 m clear of every search point); only a reported clearance or an approach probe more than 21 m out can differ

deviations.unreal: a static's footprint is its mesh bounds through its transform, its axes projected to the ground, the world-aligned bounds when an axis stands upright (VP:571–605)
deviations.core: the caller states each footprint as a box on the ground (`at`, `half`, `axis`) or a circle
deviations.why: meshes and transforms are the engine's; the box rule (signed distance, VP:529–537) is core's

deviations.unreal: props, buildings and plants are one kind of static with one 1 m margin
deviations.core: `prop`, `building` and `plant` each take a clearance (all 1 m by default)
deviations.why: the task names building footprints apart from props; the defaults keep Unreal's answer

deviations.unreal: a tie for the nearest names the first of statics, villagers, doors, containers, roads, pick-ups (VP:678–706)
deviations.core: a tie names the first of the obstacles in the caller's order, then roads, then pick-ups
deviations.why: only the reported `nearest` differs, never a spot or a clearance

deviations.unreal: no check (a non-finite position would settle as NaN)
deviations.core: a spot or ground height that is not a finite number is refused with `bad-spot`, by `settlePickup` and `pickupClearance` alike; a road waypoint or a settled pick-up that is not a finite point is skipped (a road is broken there, not joined across it), keeping every other index as given
deviations.why: a refusal is a decision an engine can act on

cases.name: pattern: Unreal's search, 40 rings 0.5 m apart out to 20 m, 8 to 64 points each
pattern: a caller's search (2 m out, a point per metre, 4 to 12 points)
ring 1 (0.5 m): the floor of 8 points, from +x toward +z
ring 2 (1 m): ceil(2π · 1 / 0.6) = 11 points
ring 12 (6 m): ceil(2π · 6 / 0.6) = 63 points
ring 13 (6.5 m): the ceiling of 64 points
ring 41: beyond the search, no points
pattern: a caller's ceiling below its floor is raised to the floor (12 points, at most 4)
cases.note: Every ring gets 12 points: the ceiling never undercuts the floor.

cases.name: clearance: nothing to keep off: Unreal's 1e9 cm, in metres
clearance: a prop's footprint exactly 1 m off: 0, which is clear
clearance: inside a prop's footprint: the deeper of the two sides, less 1 m
clearance: off a footprint's corner: the distance to the corner
clearance: a building turned 45 degrees: its own axes
cases.note: The axis is normalised by core; the box is 2 m along (1, 1) and 0.5 m across. The spot is on the box's mirror line, so this case does not tell the axis from its mirror: the 30-degree cases below do.

cases.name: clearance: a building turned 30 degrees, read off its end: half.x is along the axis
cases.note: The box is 2 m along (cos 30°, sin 30°) and 0.5 m across. The spot is 1.92 m along and 0.07 m across: 0.92 m past the end, so 0.08 m short of clear. Read mirrored (-30°), with x and z swapped (60°) or with half.x across the axis (120°), it would be 0.38 m clear, 0.004 m short and 0.67 m clear.

cases.name: clearance: a building turned 30 degrees, read off its side: half.z is across it
cases.note: The spot is 0.34 m back along the axis and 1.81 m across: 1.31 m off the long side, 0.31 m clear.

cases.name: clearance: a road: from its centre line, less half its width and 1 m
clearance: a road with no width is 3 m wide
clearance: a road past its last waypoint: from the end
clearance: a road broken by a waypoint that is not a point is not joined across the gap
cases.note: Two pieces, ending at (-2, 0) and (2, 0): the spot is √13 m off each end, 1.11 m clear. Joined across the gap it would be 3 m off the road, 0.5 m clear.

cases.name: clearance: a road whose two waypoints coincide is a point
clearance: a door: 0.6 m round, kept 2 m off
clearance: a villager: 0.4 m round, kept 1.5 m off
clearance: a container: 0.5 m round, kept 1 m off
clearance: a door with its own radius
clearance: a tree counts by its trunk at its pivot, not its canopy
cases.note: Canopy half 2 m: trunk 0.15 · 2 = 0.3 m, at the pivot. The spot stands under the canopy.

cases.name: clearance: a broad tree's trunk is no wider than 0.8 m
clearance: a slim tree's trunk is no narrower than 0.25 m
clearance: a bush (1 m tall) counts by its footprint
clearance: ground cover (0.3 m tall) is not kept off: an item lies in the grass
clearance: a plant with no height stated counts by its footprint
clearance: a static overhead (from 1.6 m up) is not kept off
clearance: a static flat on the ground (0.1 m high) is not kept off
clearance: CONTROL: the same overhead beam over ground 1 m higher stands at a dropped item's height
clearance: a ground piece (wider than 25 m both ways) is not kept off
clearance: CONTROL: a wall 30 m long but 0.2 m thick is
clearance: a pick-up already settled: 3 m apart
clearance: the clearance per kind is the caller's
clearance: the caller's container clearance
clearance: a settled pick-up that is not a point keeps its index; the next is named by its own
clearance: a spot that is not a point is refused
clearance: the least of several, and what it is
clearance: a tie names the first in the caller's order
settle: the spot is already clear: it stays
settle: against a prop: out to the nearest clear spot
cases.note: The crate's edge is 0.2 m off; 1.2 m clear needs ring 2 or beyond on the far side.

cases.name: settle: on a road: off it, past its edge and 1 m
settle: at a building's door: 2 m off it
cases.note: The door is on the building's front; the pick-up was authored on its step.

cases.name: settle: near a villager: 1.5 m off where it stands
settle: wedged between a tree trunk and a cauldron (the P6 cell's g4)
cases.note: The tree counts by a 0.45 m trunk; the fern beside is ground cover and does not count.

cases.name: settle: CONTROL: under the same canopy with no cauldron, it stays
settle: clear but off the walkable ground: onto it
cases.note: A walkable box 6 m by 2 m north of the spot (an engine's navmesh, stated).

cases.name: settle: against a building turned 30 degrees (a village lot): out past its own side
cases.note: The building is 6 m by 4 m, turned 30 degrees. The spot is 1.85 m along and 2.40 m across: 0.40 m past its long side, 0.60 m short of clear. It settles on ring 2.

cases.name: settle: a beam overhead is no obstacle on low ground …
settle: … and is one on ground 1 m higher
settle: walked up to from its open side: away from a wall
cases.note: The wall runs along x; the open side is +z.

cases.name: settle: the caller's clearance: a villager kept only 0.3 m off
settle: no clear spot: inside a building 44 m square, the clearest search point is named
cases.note: Refused with no-clear-spot. The clearest is the first point of the last ring, 20 m out, 3 m short of clear.

cases.name: settle: no clear spot: nothing walkable, the authored spot is the clearest
settle: no clear spot within a caller's search of 0.5 m: the clearest of ring 1
settle: CONTROL: the same with a search of 1 m finds a clear spot on ring 2
settle: no clear spot: the clearest is the clearest WALKABLE point
cases.note: Only a disc 1.2 m round (-10, 0) is walkable: the clearest is its point nearest the building's wall, (-11, 0) on ring 22.

cases.name: settle: a spot that is not a point is refused
sequence: two pick-ups authored 1 m apart: the first stays, the second moves 3 m off it
sequence: the same two in the other order: the other one stays
sequence: three in a row near a prop, each clear of those before it
sequence: a refused pick-up is held where its clearest is, and the next keeps clear of it there
cases.note: Nothing within 2 m of the first is walkable: it is refused at its own spot. The second settles on the walkable disc at (3, 0), 3 m clear of it; (2.5, 0) on ring 2 is walkable but 0.5 m short.

cases.name: sequence: a spot that is not a point settles nothing and holds nothing
cases.note: The third keeps clear of the second, named as pick-up 1: its index in pickups, where the refused first keeps its slot.
